title: The end-to-end comparison's future set continues the same world instead of a new random one
request: The owner chose to fix the test, not DCLab, after the check showed delivery's over-claim came from the future set: every restaurant kept its number and changed its behaviour.
spec: Keep the old future for rebuilding earlier runs; never change a stored result; the gate's cases stay as the gate saw them.
plan: future = the latest rows of one replica, by the kind's time column
rescore an old run on its own future
rerun the rules arm on the dev cases

decisions.decision: Fix the test, not the product
decisions.why: splitting by restaurant would pass this test and be wrong for the usual real case, where the same restaurants keep ordering

decisions.decision: Tickets span 60 days in the continued future
decisions.why: the replica's late team starts 30 days before the end; over 120 days it began after the cut

change: dclab_rnd/agent_eval/e2e/__init__.py (FUTURE), cases.py (make's future_kind, the time and id per kind, the ticket days, the duplicate drop, held_out_cases on new_seed), __main__.py (results record their future; rescore uses the old run's); dclab_rnd/bench/__init__.py (e2e_v1 in a layer); tests/test_e2e_comparison.py.

findings.defect: The future set punished honest knowledge of each restaurant.
findings.scenario: A restaurant's mean time correlated -0.02 between the table and the future, 0.42 between early and late rows of one table; delivery's real error was 9.40 against a claim of 7.79.
findings.cause: the future was the replica drawn with another seed: same ids, new behaviour
findings.fix: the future is the latest rows of one replica

findings.defect: The ticket future held a team no table had.
findings.scenario: Every seed: 0 rows of the late team in the table, 24 to 41 in the future; every arm scored F1 0 on it.
findings.cause: the late team starts 30 days before the replica's end, after the cut over 120 days
findings.fix: tickets span 60 days so the cut falls inside the team's window

findings.defect: A duplicate ticket could sit on both sides of the cut.
findings.scenario: Held-out seed 104: one ticket_id in both the table and the future.
findings.cause: the cut is a row position and duplicates share their time
findings.fix: a future row whose id the table holds is dropped

findings.defect: The gate's cases would be rebuilt on a future it was not judged on, and the rescore rule had no real test.
findings.scenario: held_out_cases built continued futures; E2E-004 was judged on new_seed.
findings.fix: held_out_cases builds new_seed; the rescore test checks the future through the command

measurements.name: The rules arm on the six dev cases, new_seed (E2E-007) against continued (E2E-009)
measurements.result: delivery: real 9.40 to 8.14 minutes, claimed 7.79 to 7.30, inside interval 0 to 1 of 3; tickets: real 0.387 to 0.388, claimed 0.403 both, inside interval 3 to 2 of 3
measurements.next: score each arm's own model on the future set, so a claim and its real score come from the same model
limits: the real score refits one reference model, not the arm's own

outcome: The comparison's future now continues the same world; delivery's real error fell from 9.40 to 8.14 minutes. A claim about 0.8 minutes too good remains, possibly from the scorer's reference model.
lessons: Before changing a product to pass a test, check whether the test matches real use.
A cut in time can hide a class that appears late: check every class on both sides.
risks: Runs before and after the change are not comparable number for number.
